Quick triage summary (prelim):

What we see
- p95 TTFT: baseline ~80ms, current ~430ms (increase ~350ms).
- p99 TTFT: baseline ~210ms, current ~1410ms (increase ~1.2s).
- Error rate for small, short requests (<=64 tokens) increased by ~2.3x.
- CDN edge metrics show a sharp increase in TLS handshake duration and handshake retries starting 2026-12-01 21:40 UTC.

Root cause hypothesis
- Upstream edge (CDN -> our origin layer) shows elevated SYN retransmissions and reduced TCP connection reuse. That leads to more full TLS handshakes rather than session resumption. In practice, this manifests as extra RTTs before first byte is emitted.
- Recent CDN config rollback (ticket CDN-5677) reduced session cache TTLs and disabled a session-ticket optimization on several POPs ~2026-12-01 20:55 UTC — FRA and LON POPs most affected.

Immediate mitigations applied (done within last 4 hours)
- Forced routing for OmniCart traffic away from FRA POP to neighboring POPs with healthy session caches.
- Re-enabled session-ticket support for affected POPs (temporary config override).
- Increased TLS session cache size on origin-facing layer.

Next steps (48h plan)
- Work with CDN partner to restore stable session ticket behavior and revert the config rollback permanently.
- Add defensive routing rules for customers with elevated p99 to avoid affected POPs automatically.
- Collect full pcap and correlate with SYN/ACK retransmission windows for postmortem.

Attachments: p95_graph.png (summary graph), preliminary notes to include tcpdump-snippet.txt.

Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime

Alex — thanks again for raising this and for the packet samples. Quick customer update and plan:

Status (short):
- Root cause: regression in CDN session-resumption behavior after a config rollback; this increased full TLS handshakes on affected POPs and amplified upstream SYN retransmissions, causing elevated first-byte latency (p95/p99).
- Current state: temporary mitigations in place (forced routing away from affected POPs, re-enabled session tickets on impacted POPs, increased origin session cache). These reduced overall p95 by ~260ms; p99 still sees intermittent spikes as the CDN partner finishes global config stabilization.

Customer-facing ETA and actions:
- Immediate (done): routing override for OmniCart + session-ticket re-enable. Visible improvement in most regions.
- 24–72 hours: CDN partner to roll forward permanent config (coordination in progress), we'll add automated POP shielding for affected customers.
- Post-incident: full postmortem and corrective actions (within 7 business days).

Goodwill proposal: Redwood will provide a one-time credit for the confirmed incident window. Monica will propose specific credit terms and follow up with Procurement/Legal.

We will send a short status note formatted for your customers within 2 hours; please let us know if you want any specific wording or if we should copy your CSM.
